data.long_meaning: Kanji is a Sanskrit name derived from the term 'Kan' meaning 'Lord' and 'Ji' meaning 'Gods'. This name represents the supreme deity in Hindu mythology, Lord Shiva, who is the ruler of all gods. It is a powerful and spiritual name, evoking feelings of strength, power, and divinity. The name Kanji carries the meaning “Lord of Gods” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Kanji usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of gods and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Kanji Stambh (Pillar of Kanji) - A significant historical monument located at Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh. The inscription on the pillar dates back to 1153 AD and mentions the name of a king named Kanha or Kanji.

Kanji Bhatt - A 14th-century Jain monk and scholar from Gujarat. He wrote commentaries on various Jain texts and authored several original works. Most notable among his works is the 'Sarvadharma-Samgraha', which is a synopsis of all major religious and philosophical systems of his time.

This trend can be seen on Instagram, where there are numerous posts showcasing the preparation and presentation of this dish.
